lead: four people earn their living inside a place your hands made — the benches, the wiring, the machine that has no business still running — and nobody inside has been shown the arrangement that keeps it standing.
sun: this cover got built by hand and goes on being built by hand: a bench replaced without discussion, a job taken in at a price you never checked, a repair done at seven in the morning so the day can start clean. none of that is on show, and no one who works there could say what the place costs to keep, because no account of it has ever been read aloud.
moon: the making does not keep a count. a thing needed on tuesday exists by thursday and goes across the bench with no figure attached, and that ability is the single point of contact holding the whole place off the ground. skill does not sag first. it works at full speed until the morning a wrist or an eye stops obliging, and then it is a room with tools in it.
pull: everything in there came out of the same two hands, and those hands are the arrangement — no ledger, no second maker, and no version of the place that outlasts your wrists.
tension: what gets said about you is that you are handy, which is affectionate and about a fifth true. the four of them price their own work fluently and have no figure for yours, so what you put in arrives at zero and gets budgeted there, year after year. who repairs the repairer has never come up in that building, because raising it needs somebody to have looked under the cover, and the cover is the thing you built best.
cost: the compressor was down at six and running by nine, and the people upstairs never learned there had been an hour without it, so the place has no bad month it can name. the same habit of doing it before anyone is up leaves no record to consult, so the morning your hands stop it goes down in one piece and they find out by standing in the weather.

lead: the work is out where anybody can take it, and what it earns is a room each for five people, two of whom had run out of rooms. nobody who admires it in public knows the second sentence exists.
sun: the shelter you put up runs on what the work brings in — rent, a standing order, an address that can be given to a hospital. that arrangement never comes up, because the visible thing answers every question anyone thinks to ask and closes the conversation before it gets near the rest. and it stands on one item only: the work continuing to earn at roughly this rate.
moon: The Jewel sends it out with nothing held back: the method travels with the object, every step of the working, your name across the top, and arming it against anything never once presents itself as a task. so what five people are living off is what anybody in the trade can lift, and admiration and copying arrive down the same road looking identical for about a year.
pull: the thing is out in the light with no guard on it, and five people sleep under what it pays for, and those two facts have never been in the same room as each other.
tension: you get read as somebody with a good year behind them and no dependents, which is what the visible half looks like. the ones it houses have learned not to raise it, since raising it means looking under, and you have never lifted it for anybody. when a larger outfit ships the same idea with lawyers attached, the argument that stops them requires showing what is at stake, and that is the one thing you will not show.
cost: an idea leaves you complete, method attached, nothing withheld, and it travels further in eighteen months than a guarded version manages in ten years — which is the entire reason there is anything to house anybody with. no guard on it also means the roof over five people is one competent copy away from gone, in one piece, on a day none of them will see coming.

lead: directions to it work at midnight from two towns away — anybody can send anybody. directions to you do not exist in any form, and the place stands on you and nothing else.
sun: you put it up deliberately and it is standing: rooms allocated, a way in that people pass to each other, somebody in there tonight who had nowhere in particular to be a year ago. what happens under it is nobody's to examine, and that was never a policy — no part of the arrangement was written down in a form anybody could ask to see.
moon: The Veil takes the person who built that and attaches them to nothing. no group doing the same work claims you, no organisation carries your name, no one can state where you stand in relation to the thing you made. you are not concealed — everyone inside knows your face and your hours. you cannot be located from outside at any address except the door itself.
pull: no register anywhere carries the arrangement, and no list anywhere carries you, and eleven people are asleep under it tonight all the same.
tension: the ones who came through want to give something back and cannot work out where it goes; the place takes a rota slot and nothing else, and you are not standing anywhere a debt could be paid to. anybody official needs a person to hold responsible, finds a working arrangement with no one attached to it, and files that as evasion — the single reading of you that is completely wrong, and the one your position hands out.
cost: nothing had to be cleared with anybody, so the second house was occupied in nine days while a funded body was still deciding whether it had the remit, and that speed comes straight out of belonging to nothing. the whole of it therefore rests on someone nobody can point to, with no seam to attach a second, so it ends the day you are unavailable, entire, without notice.

lead: notices have been arriving for two years, at your address, which was arranged. the fourteen people they concern have been told nothing, and what is being defended is partly that — their not knowing.
sun: the fight is run out of sight of the people it is about, and what they live under is the thing being fought for. what is in there is not available for inspection, which is your best asset here and your worst exposure at once: the other side is disputing an arrangement it has never seen, and the paper that would settle this outright would put fourteen names on a desk in an office.
moon: neither grip has ever been loosened. giving ground outward to keep the evenings inside calm has been available for two years and never once picked up; nor has the reverse. both close at the same weight and stay closed, which is why this is in its third year, and why neither the solicitor nor the person who shares your kitchen can get you to name the one you would drop.
pull: two arguments carried at full weight by one person, all of it standing on you staying upright between them — and if either hand opens, everyone under the cover learns everything that afternoon.
tension: stubborn from one end and evasive from the other, and each of them is looking at half of it. what neither can be shown is why the settlement on the table is not one: it stops the letters, and it requires the arrangement to be described room by room to people who would then hold a list. so it stays live, at your own expense, in a shape nobody has agreed to and nobody can audit.
cost: a dispute that would have flattened somebody carrying one side of it has gone into a fourth year without a single person inside losing an ordinary week, and that outcome is rare enough that the solicitor has remarked on it. holding both means no version of this finishes early, and on the day the one support gives, both hands are still full, and it goes with both arguments still live.
